headline: Schwarber sinks the Sox while the Patriots reveal their fall schedule
morning_brew: The bats went silent again at Fenway Park last night. Kyle Schwarber hit his eighteenth home run of the year to break our hearts in the eighth inning, and it was a total punch to the gut. Ranger Suarez was actually dealing, throwing five and a third innings with eight strikeouts and no runs allowed. But you cannot win games in this league when the lineup only manages one run on seven hits. Tyler Samaniego had a rough outing in relief and took the loss. It is a tough pill to swallow after a decent win the night before.

We finally have the roadmap for the fall after the team revealed the schedule at Six Flags. Opening the season against the Seahawks is an interesting draw for Drake Maye and the new look squad. Nine international games across the league is a lot of travel, but we just want to see the divisional matchups and when the Jets come to town. Betting odds for Week One are already out. It feels like football season even if it is only May.

Things are quiet at the Garden with both the B's and C's watching the playoffs from home after those early exits. There is plenty of talk about Giannis trade scenarios, but that is just offseason noise until something actually happens. We are looking at a long summer of roster building for both teams. I been watchin' this team since seventy-eight, and the offseason always feels twice as long when you exit in the first round. We need a guy who wants to be here and can actually close out a series.
